en: Solid ice is matter because it has mass and takes up space, even though it floats on liquid water.
Liquid water evaporates into a gas at room temperature, so it does not need to reach a boiling point to change states.
Melting a solid chocolate bar into a liquid is a physical change because no new chemical substance is created.
Dissolving solid sugar in water does not destroy the sugar, as the sugar molecules remain intact but spread throughout the liquid.
Invisible air inside a balloon has measurable mass, proving that gases are matter even though we cannot see them.
Iron rusting is a chemical change because the metal reacts with oxygen to form a completely new brown substance.
Pure liquid distilled water is not a solution because it contains only one type of molecule instead of a mixture.
Burning a piece of paper does not destroy matter, but transforms it into new substances like ash and carbon dioxide gas.
Aluminum and copper are solid metals, but they are not magnetic and will not stick to a refrigerator magnet.
Water droplets on a cold glass form from invisible water vapor in the outside air condensing, not from liquid leaking through.
The bubbles in boiling water are filled with water vapor gas, not air trapped inside the liquid.
Pouring saltwater through filter paper cannot separate the mixture because the dissolved salt particles are too small to be caught.
